recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-20572; any future recurrence should be handled in the validator/IG Publisher tooling stream unless a later work-group decision changes the discriminator rules.
issue_request: FHIR-20572 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction, raised against STU3 and applied for R5, reporting that the IG Publisher validator returned an informational message that it could not find a slice when an Observation.component slice was distinguished by a value discriminator on code and the sliced code element carried a required value-set binding.
initial_application: No source commit tagged with FHIR-20572 and no current source occurrence of the issue key were found. FHIR-I minutes from 2020-01-27 record Grahame Grieve saying the issue was fixed, and the current R5/R6 core source reflects the adjacent rule needed for this scenario: value discrimination can be based on a required value set binding, with the deprecated pattern discriminator equivalent to value.
additional_context: The seed is a tooling/validator behavior report rather than a request for new normative prose. Related Published issue FHIR-25206, already represented on the combined branch, records the broader decision to merge value and pattern discriminator semantics and allow required value-set bindings as value discriminators. FHIR-34152, also already represented, supplied later profiling prose that explicitly says value discrimination can use a fixed value, pattern value, or required value set binding. No later conflicting community, Jira, source, or git evidence was found.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current build-scoped Profiling FHIR and ElementDefinition sources already convey the rule needed by the reported validator behavior, and the direct work-group evidence says the validator issue was fixed.

related_jiras.note: Broader Published decision to make value/pattern discriminator semantics allow required value-set bindings; already represented on the combined branch and not decided again here.
